source.text: ርኢኩ፡ ዘዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ነፋሳተ፡ ዘይጸውር፡ †በደመናት፤ ርኢኩ፡ ፍናወ፡ መላእክት፤ ርኢኩ፡ ውስተ፡ ጽንፈ፡ ምድር፡ ጽንዐ፡ ዘሰማይ፡ መልዕልተ።
source.note: Diplomatic selected Geʽez from actual Charles1906 printed48/PDF86 or printed50/PDF88. Actual critical dagger signs retained, raised apparatus references omitted and punctuation spacing normalized. The English choice at each corrupt locus, including diplomatic retention instead of adoption, is identified below. It is not represented as a restored original text or a fresh manuscript collation.

additional_translation_input.edition: R. H. Charles, The Ethiopic Version of the Book of Enoch,1906, with edited Greek parallel/apparatus
additional_translation_input.reported_witness_labels: t, β (Charles printed48 note19); later Ethiopic MSS (printed49 note6)
additional_translation_input.english_scope: Clouds is construed as the object of carrying; no new object such as earth/heaven is supplied.
additional_translation_input.textual_reason: Selected prepositional bearing clause is explicitly corrupt. The reported no-preposition variant gives the carrying verb a cloud object and produces a readable clause without inventing an unattested noun.

translation.text: I saw the winds over the earth carrying the clouds.[a] I saw the paths of the angels. At the edge of the earth I saw the firmament of heaven above.

footnotes.text: The selected Geʽez prints the corrupt bearing expression with †በደመናት, “in clouds,” leaving its object unclear. This English adopts the object “clouds” from the later Ethiopic variant reported by Charles, not from an invented missing object: printed48 note19 reports ደመናት without the preposition for t and β, and printed49 note6 describes the later reading as Greek-equivalent τὰς νεφέλας, “the clouds,” contrasting the best Ethiopic evidence. The printed singular bearing form and plural winds are also awkward. The selected source is preserved unchanged; the English is an explicit critical reading, not a claim that the best selected manuscripts all say “carrying the clouds.” I inspected Charles’s report, not those manuscripts themselves.

source.text: ወእሳተ፡ ዘይነድድ፡ ርኢኩ፡ †ወዘሀሎ፡ ውስተ፡ ኵሉ፡ አድባር።†

additional_translation_input.english_scope: No Greek replacement adopted in running English. Greek identifies the corrupt history disclosed in the note; the selected within-all clause is rendered diplomatically.
additional_translation_input.textual_reason: Retain a readable selected-edition second-object construction rather than impose an unmarked Greek substitution or attach beyond-these-mountains to the fire without resolving its connection to18:10.

translation.text: I saw burning fire and what lay within all the mountains.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected daggered clause literally has “and what was within all the mountains,” retained here as a second object of seeing. It is readable as a diplomatic construction but not certified as the earlier meaning. Charles printed48 note51, continued on49, identifies it as a corrupt rendering of the Greek κἀπέκεινα τῶν ὀρέων τούτων, “and beyond these mountains,” and calls “all” corrupt for “these.” That Greek location phrase also leads into the place description of18:10. This English does not silently replace within with beyond or all with these, or force the location phrase to modify the fire. The printed Greek is comparison evidence, not a newly collated manuscript.

additional_translation_input.english_scope: The corrupt spirit/asking relation is rendered as the speaker asking about the seven stars; English coordination replaces the Greek participial link to18:14.
additional_translation_input.textual_reason: The selected clause reverses/incoherently renders the inquiry; the actual Greek participle and first-person dative μοι provide the inquiry relation rather than an invented request from a spirit.

translation.text: There I saw seven stars like great burning mountains, and I asked about them.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected final Geʽez clause is daggered and corrupt, approximately “and like a spirit that asks me,” with the direction of inquiry distorted. The English inquiry about the stars adopts Charles’s printed Greek περὶ ὧν πυνθανομένῳ μοι, “as I inquired about them.” His printed50 note24 and printed51 note5 explicitly compare the corrupt Geʽez with this inquiry construction. The Greek links the inquiry to the angel’s reply in18:14; English coordinates “I asked” for a readable verse without adding the reply here. This is an openly Greek-assisted critical treatment, not a claim that the selected Geʽez spirit-asks-me clause is sound or that a Greek manuscript was independently collated.

additional_translation_input.english_scope: Duration ten thousand years replaces corrupt year-of-mystery in English only; the selected sin/completion wording remains.
additional_translation_input.textual_reason: The duration is explicitly corrupt in the selected edition and the primary Greek has years with the myriad numeral, while the Geʽez mystery word is independently confirmed as a nonnumeric loanword.

translation.text: He was angry with them and bound them until the time when their sin would come to an end—for ten thousand years.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected ending literally has “in a year of mystery,” with “mystery” daggered. Dillmann1865 col181 confirms the mystery/secret word and explicitly cites18:16; it does not mean ten thousand. For the duration this English adopts Charles’s printed Greek ἐνιαυτῶν μυρίων, ten thousand years. Printed50 note36 and printed51 note9 identify the Geʽez ending as corrupt and distinguish Greek years/myriad from year/mystery. The duration therefore comes from the explicitly identified edited Greek parallel, not from silently changing a Geʽez numeral, lexicalizing mystery as a number, or claiming fresh manuscript evidence. “Sin” retains the selected noun rather than replacing it with an unmarked word for punishment.
